Reassessing the June 10, 2020 FOMC statement with relevant literature: The Fed’s emphasis on “considerable risks” to growth and jobs is consistent with evidence that pandemics trigger simultaneous demand and supply-chain shocks and sharply elevate economic policy uncertainty, all of which depress real activity (COVID-19 production/consumption and supply-chain shocks; uncertainty spikes during pandemics). Offsetting this, the commitment to the zero lower bound, continued large-scale purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS/CMBS, and ample repo operations strengthens transmission via financial markets and credit channels; research on forward guidance and inflation-forecast targeting (Svensson and Woodford) and on the financial accelerator (Bernanke-Gertler-Gilchrist) finds such measures can lower term premia, ease spreads, and stabilize credit even at the ZLB. That said, some studies find QE’s real-growth impact is limited, tempering the positive impulse. With muted inflation pressures and anchored expectations, the policy stance mitigates but does not neutralize the predominantly cautious tone.
